provenance.purpose: Retained authored records for review #35, #37 and #63

cases.sentence: O livro que a Ana comprou desapareceu.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The sentence means that the book Ana bought disappeared. The unpunctuated relative clause is analyzed as a restrictive modifier of livro. In this derivation, que is an overt relative operator originating as the object of comprou, rather than a complementizer accompanied by a silent operator. External Merge combines comprou with que and independently combines the article a with Ana. The remaining lexical and functional objects are available for subsequent Merge. Node labels identify projecting heads in Bare Phrase Structure; they do not introduce an independently stipulated X-bar template. The finite verbs are lexical items already bearing their inflection, so their spellings do not require separate morphological realization groups.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the relative clause's object position and lexical resources.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The transitive light verb merges with the previously constructed verbal object, and the nominal a Ana merges as its external argument. The resulting object projects v and supplies the agent of buying. Que remains in its original complement position; neither the verb nor either argument has moved yet.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce Ana as the relative clause's external argument.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Comprou raises from the established V position into the transitive light verb, creating a complex head. Its lower occurrence becomes unpronounced. Que then undergoes Internal Merge at the outer edge of the transitive v domain, outside the agent. This intermediate occurrence is required by the phase-based analysis: subsequent relative extraction must proceed from the accessible edge rather than directly from the transferred verbal complement. The lower object copy is unpronounced, while the edge copy temporarily carries que's pronunciation. Finite T subsequently merges above this completed v object. Head movement and operator movement have independent targets; both precede this Merge of T.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the relative verb to v and evacuate the relative operator to the phase edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The complex verbal head raises from v to T; its v-position occurrence becomes silent and comprou is pronounced in the higher complex head. T agrees with a Ana, licensing nominative Case and third-person singular agreement. The subject then undergoes Internal Merge to the edge of T, producing the preverbal subject order. For subject A-movement, this analysis uses a silent nominal trace at the source rather than a fully articulated lower copy. The pronounced nominal's article and name persist in the higher occurrence. Que remains at the v edge, awaiting the relative complementizer.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the relative clause's finite inflectional domain.

values.interpretation: property of things that Ana bought

derivationStages.stageRecord: The silent relative C merges with the finite relative clause. Its relative edge requirement attracts que from the previously established v-edge occurrence. The resulting C-labeled object has the overt operator at its edge; both earlier operator occurrences are silent. The operator binds the buying event's object position, giving the clause a property interpretation suitable for nominal modification. The pronounced order of the completed relative is que a Ana comprou. This external-head analysis does not raise livro out of the relative clause.

The completed relative clause adjoins to the nominal livro, preserving N as the label of the modified object. The relative property restricts the noun's denotation before O merges to form the definite nominal. Desapareceu then selects this nominal as its internal theme. Disappearance is analyzed as unaccusative: the book is not introduced as an agent or as an external argument. Consequently, its eventual matrix-subject position must be derived from the internal argument position now shown.
derivationStages.statement: Build the modified book nominal and merge it as the argument of desaparecer.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The unaccusative light verb merges with the matrix verbal object. Unlike the relative clause's transitive v, this head introduces no external argument and is treated as nonphasal for extraction of the internal nominal. The book nominal remains the complement of the lexical verb. This workspace supplies the head configuration from which the matrix verb will raise.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the matrix unaccusative v domain without an external argument.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Desapareceu raises from its established V position into the unaccusative light verb. The lower verb occurrence becomes silent, and the higher occurrence retains the whole-word realization desapareceu. Finite T then merges above the v domain. The complex v head is now an explicitly available source for subsequent head movement to T; the book nominal has not yet left its internal argument position.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the matrix verb to v and introduce finite T.

values.movedDomain: entire definite nominal including its relative modifier

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix complex verb raises from v to T, leaving its lower occurrences silent. T agrees with the singular definite book nominal and licenses nominative Case. The entire nominal, including its already completed restrictive relative, then undergoes A-movement from the internal argument position to the edge of T. As in the relative subject dependency, the source is represented by a silent nominal trace, while the nominal's internal structure persists in the higher occurrence. This movement is not extraction from inside the relative clause: the relative travels as part of the whole nominal. Finally, silent declarative C merges with the completed finite clause. The pronounced tree order is exactly O livro que a Ana comprou desapareceu. The supplied final punctuation marks the utterance boundary and is not an additional syntactic token.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the matrix subject dependency and the declarative sentence.

values.interpretation: The recipient is restricted to Younghee among the contextually relevant alternatives.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The analysis uses head-final X-bar projections and a Government and Binding derivation with a VP-internal subject. 민수 and 책 project NPs whose nominal heads contain the overt case suffixes 가 and 을. These suffixes are present morphologically, but their structural Case licensing awaits the relevant clause structure. 영희 projects the complement NP of the postposition 에게, which assigns inherent dative Case. The restrictive particle 만 projects a particle phrase right-adjoined to this PP; it restricts the recipient, yielding 'only to Younghee', rather than modifying the theme or the entire clause. Each of these three expressions is associated with its supplied input token despite containing multiple morphological terminals. The verb 주, the finite inflection containing past 었 and declarative 다, and a silent declarative C are selected separately. This analysis treats 다 as a finite ending within I and does not require verb movement to C. The verbal pieces are not yet associated collectively with 주었다.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the nominal expressions, focused recipient, and verbal inflection.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb first combines with the theme NP 책을 to form the lower V′. A higher V′ introduces the selected recipient PP 영희에게만, and the subject NP 민수가 occupies Spec-VP. The recursive V′ structure accommodates the two internal arguments without introducing an additional light verb: the theme is the lower complement and the recipient is the higher internal argument. The focus particle remains inside the recipient constituent and does not change its thematic role. 주 assigns Theme to 책, Goal to the dative expression, and Agent to 민수. Under the adopted GB government configuration, the verb governs the theme NP within its VP and licenses accusative Case, matching 을. The subject's nominative morphology is still awaiting licensing by finite I.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the ditransitive VP and establish its argument structure.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The finite I head takes the completed VP as its complement, producing a head-final I′ inside IP. Spec-IP is not yet filled: 민수가 remains in its independently established Agent position in Spec-VP. This intermediate structure supplies the local target for subsequent V-to-I movement and the landing position for subject A-movement. Past tense and declarative finiteness are represented in I, but no verbal morphological realization is established yet because the lexical verb remains separate from its endings. The silent C remains outside the clause until the completed IP is available.

The lexical V moves from the lower V′ head position to the immediately superordinate I head. A silent head trace replaces its earlier position, while the raised V adjoins to the left of the inflectional head, yielding the head-final morphological order 주–었–다. This is an explicit V-to-I implementation of Korean verbal inflection, not a claim that the word order alone uniquely forces that implementation. The movement obeys the Head Movement Constraint because no intervening head separates V from I; the recursive V′ nodes are projections, not intervening heads. The verb's trace preserves its argument and accusative-licensing position. Once the complex finite head exists, its three morphological terminals are collectively associated with input token 주었다. The subject remains in Spec-VP, so its movement is recorded separately.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the verb to I and establish the finite verbal realization.

relations.relation: local A-binding of the subject trace

derivationStages.stageRecord: The subject NP moves from its recorded Spec-VP position to Spec-IP, leaving a silent NP trace. Its upper occurrence receives nominative Case from finite I, realized by 가, and satisfies the requirement for a clausal subject. The chain receives exactly one theta-role, Agent, through its lower position; Spec-IP is a non-theta position. The raised subject locally c-commands and binds its trace, satisfying the GB requirement that an NP trace be locally A-bound. No scrambling is posited: the recipient precedes the theme in the base VP, and subject raising preserves the supplied subject–recipient–theme–verb order. The silent declarative C then takes the completed IP as its complement, producing a head-final CP. The resulting reading is that Minsu gave a book, or the contextually identified book, only to Younghee. That contextual choice for the bare noun does not require a second syntactic structure. The realization associations now cover all four input tokens; neither movement trace nor the null C contributes pronunciation.
derivationStages.statement: Complete subject A-movement, nominative licensing, and the declarative CP.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The relative predicate ver ‘give’ projects a head-final VP with a dative recipient and an unpronounced object operator in its Theme position. The Agent, Öğretmenin, is base-generated in the nominalized clause's subject position, Spec-IP. The nominal inflectional head contains the nominalizer -DIK and third-person singular possessive agreement; together they license the genitive subject. Here Öğretmenin is therefore ‘the teacher’s’, not the homographic nominative expression ‘your teacher’, which would require additional genitive marking in this construction. Öğrencilere is the dative recipient. The relative clause's nominal inflection is not a finite past-tense head: the giving event's temporal interpretation is contextual. Kitaplar, the unaccusative matrix predicate kaybol ‘disappear’, and the matrix past-tense inflection remain separate objects. Whole-word nominal terminals already have their input associations; verbal stems and affixes have not yet received their collective surface realizations.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the relative clause's underlying argument structure and the remaining lexical material.

values.movement: left adjunction of V to nominal I

derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb moves from its previously established VP position to the nominal inflectional head, leaving a head trace. Left adjunction to the head-final inflectional complex places the verb before the nominalizer and possessive agreement. This complex receives the collective realization verdiği through Turkish suffix allomorphy, vowel harmony, and intervocalic softening of the nominalizer's final consonant. The lexical verb and both suffixes remain distinct syntactic contributors. The null operator is still in the object position, so its later movement will begin from a position explicitly present in this workspace.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the relative verb into nominal inflection and establish the realization verdiği.

values.licensing: local government through the verbal head chain

values.interpretation: books that the teacher gives or gave to the students

derivationStages.stageRecord: A head-final CP is projected over the nominalized IP with an unpronounced relative complementizer. The null operator moves from its object position to Spec-CP, leaving an NP trace and forming an A-bar chain. Its object trace retains the Theme interpretation and abstract accusative Case supplied by the relative verb chain; local verbal government licenses this argument trace. The CP is adjoined to the left of the nominal projection headed by kitaplar. Relative predication links that external head to the operator without treating the head noun as an occurrence moved out of the relative clause. The resulting modified NP is then merged as the internal Theme of the unaccusative matrix verb. No matrix external Agent is introduced.
derivationStages.statement: Form the object relative, attach it to kitaplar, and establish the matrix Theme position.

children.label: NP: null relative operator in Spec-CP

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix VP combines with the previously separate finite inflectional head to form a head-final IP. Because kaybol is unaccusative, its internal Theme cannot obtain structural accusative Case from the verb. The entire relative-modified NP therefore raises from the complement position shown in the preceding stage to Spec-IP, leaving an NP trace. Finite inflection licenses nominative Case on the raised NP, and the A-chain preserves its internal Theme role. The relative CP remains inside the moving NP; neither its operator nor its genitive subject moves into the matrix clause. The matrix verb remains in its lexical position at this stage, keeping NP movement distinct from the subsequent head movement and surface realization.
derivationStages.statement: Build the finite matrix IP and raise its internal argument to subject position.

children.label: NP: null relative operator in Spec-CP

values.movement: left adjunction of V to finite I

values.compatibility: Turkish permits nonplural verbal agreement with this inanimate plural subject

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix verb raises from its established VP position and left-adjoins to finite I, leaving a head trace. The stem kaybol and past suffix -DI collectively realize kayboldu; the third-person singular/default agreement exponent is zero. This agreement form is compatible with the inanimate plural subject kitaplar and does not make that subject syntactically singular. The completed matrix clause is represented as a root IP because the input provides no overt matrix complementizer or independent evidence requiring a further CP layer. The resulting pronunciation is Öğretmenin öğrencilere verdiği kitaplar kayboldu: the teacher is the genitive subject of the embedded giving predicate, the students are its recipients, and the relative-modified books are the Theme and surface subject of the past-tense disappearance predicate. Both movement chains retain their silent traces, and the relative operator remains unpronounced.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the matrix inflection and the surface analysis of the sentence.
